title: GuideAI: A Real-time Personalized Learning Solution with Adaptive Interventions
venue: 31st International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '26)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a key limitation of current LLM-based learning tools: although they can explain content and answer questions, they typically do not adapt to learners’ real-time cognitive, attentional, or physiological states. The authors argue that existing AI tutors are largely text-centric and reactive, missing signals such as stress, cognitive load, fatigue, and disengagement that influence learning effectiveness. To motivate the system design, they first conducted a formative survey with 66 participants about AI learning-tool use, perceived limitations, preferred modalities, and desired personalization features.

The intervention studied is GuideAI, a web-based personalized learning system that integrates a large language model with real-time biosensory and behavioral inputs. GuideAI uses eye tracking, heart rate variability, posture monitoring, and note-taking analysis to infer learner states such as cognitive load, attention, stress, fatigue, engagement, and understanding. Based on these signals, it adapts content, pacing, tone, and intervention type across text, image, audio, and video learning modes. The system can simplify explanations, restructure content, redirect attention, offer breathing prompts, provide posture reminders, and vary challenge level when learners appear under- or over-challenged.

The empirical evaluation was a preliminary within-subject controlled study with 25 participants from undergraduate, master's, and doctoral backgrounds, plus a prior formative assessment including students, educators, and professionals in learning-focused roles. Participants interacted with both GuideAI and a non-adaptive standard LLM baseline in a controlled lab-like setup using biosensors. Learning topics came from STEM-related domains such as statistics, machine learning, and biology. Outcomes included standardized knowledge assessments, NASA-TLX cognitive-load ratings, subjective Likert-scale evaluations, qualitative feedback, and an ablation study of intervention types.

The main conclusion is that GuideAI outperformed the non-personalized baseline on several short-term outcomes. Participants showed statistically significant improvements in problem-solving and some recall measures, along with reduced mental demand, effort, and frustration and higher perceived performance. Subjective ratings also favored GuideAI for focus, personalization, pacing, and perceived learning. At the same time, the authors frame the work as preliminary: they note limitations related to small sample size, sensor-heavy deployment requirements, privacy concerns, possible LLM hallucinations, and lack of long-term follow-up, and they call for broader and more scalable future evaluations.

identified_tools.name: GuideAI
identified_tools.description: A biosensor-augmented, multimodal personalized learning system that integrates LLM-based instruction with real-time eye tracking, heart-rate variability, posture, and note-taking signals to infer learner state and adapt content, pacing, tone, and interventions.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a real-time adaptive learning platform across text-, image-, audio-, and video-based STEM learning tasks, compared within-subjects against a non-adaptive standard LLM baseline.

findings.finding_summary: In a preliminary within-subjects study, GuideAI improved problem-solving performance across modalities by a mean of 16.5 percentage points relative to the non-adaptive control (n=25). Reported scores were Text 75% vs 52%, Image 78% vs 48%, Audio 70% vs 59% (p < 0.05), and Video 72% vs 68% (not significant).
findings.measure: Problem-solving assessment scores (%) across text, image, audio, and video learning modes

findings.finding_summary: GuideAI improved recall performance by a mean of 10.3 percentage points across modalities (n=25). Reported recall scores were Image 82% vs 62% and Audio 70% vs 52% (p < 0.05), while Text 65% vs 64% and Video 72% vs 70% showed minimal differences.
findings.measure: Recall-based knowledge assessment scores (%) across learning modes

findings.finding_summary: GuideAI reduced perceived cognitive load on several NASA-TLX dimensions versus control in the preliminary study (n=25). Reported differences were lower mental demand (Δ = 0.49, p < 0.05), physical demand (Δ = 0.23, p < 0.05), effort (Δ = 0.28, p < 0.05), and frustration (Δ = 0.54, p < 0.05), alongside higher perceived performance (Δ = 0.34, p < 0.05).
findings.measure: NASA-TLX ratings: mental demand, physical demand, effort, frustration, and perceived performance
findings.effect_size: Δ mental demand = 0.49; Δ physical demand = 0.23; Δ effort = 0.28; Δ frustration = 0.54; Δ performance = 0.34

findings.finding_summary: Learning mode-specific NASA-TLX results showed GuideAI lowered load in several modalities but increased temporal demand in video learning (n=25). Text-based learning reduced mental demand (Δ = 0.65, p < 0.05) and temporal demand (Δ = 0.96, p < 0.05); image-based reduced mental demand (Δ = 0.51, p < 0.05) and temporal demand (Δ = 0.59, p < 0.05); audio-based increased perceived performance (Δ = 0.77, p < 0.05) and reduced frustration (Δ = 1.14, p < 0.05); video-based reduced physical demand (Δ = 0.33, p < 0.05) but had higher temporal demand (Δ = 0.60, p < 0.05).
findings.effect_size: Text: Δ mental demand = 0.65, Δ temporal demand = 0.96; Image: Δ mental demand = 0.51, Δ temporal demand = 0.59; Audio: Δ performance = 0.77, Δ frustration = 1.14; Video: Δ physical demand = 0.33, Δ temporal demand = 0.60

findings.finding_summary: Participants rated GuideAI significantly higher than control on several subjective learning experience measures (n=25). Significant differences were found for focus and attention (GuideAI M=5.60, SD=1.25 vs Control M=4.85, SD=1.34, p=0.0418), content personalization (5.55, SD=1.32 vs 4.90, SD=1.26, p=0.0362), adaptive pacing (5.40, SD=1.28 vs 4.65, SD=1.22, p=0.0322), and perceived learning (5.50, SD=1.16 vs 4.75, SD=1.18, p=0.0402).
findings.measure: 7-point Likert ratings for focus, personalization, adaptive pacing, and perceived learning
findings.effect_size: Focus d=-0.48; Personalization d=-0.45; Adaptive pacing d=-0.47; Perceived learning d=-0.49

findings.finding_summary: Within the GuideAI condition, participants rated the intervention system positively on responsiveness, engagement, and performance support. Reported means were responsiveness M=5.50, SD=0.75; engagement M=5.33, SD=0.47; positive task performance impact M=5.25, SD=0.58; personalization M=5.00, SD=0.66; conceptual clarity M=4.71, SD=0.68; and adjustment based on mistakes/struggles M=4.43, SD=0.55.
findings.measure: GuideAI-only intervention evaluation on 7-point Likert scales

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-family language model product used for text, vision, and speech generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as component models inside the GuideAI platform and the baseline system: gpt-4o-mini for dialogue, gpt-4o for vision-based note analysis, and gpt-4o-mini-tts for audio responses.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods preliminary study with a within-subjects comparison (n=25), but it is small-scale and not presented as a rigorous randomized controlled trial with full credibility details. The evidence is stronger than a pure prototype description but still preliminary.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports consistent positive effects, including mean gains of 16.5 percentage points in problem-solving and 10.3 percentage points in recall, plus significant NASA-TLX improvements. However, standardized effect sizes for the main academic outcomes are not reported, so impact appears modest-to-promising rather than definitively large.
